attack_surfaces.input: username (0x20 bytes) and guesses (0x100 bytes) from stdin
attack_surfaces.operation: read() return value used as array index without bounds check; no NUL termination if buffer filled exactly
attack_surfaces.reason: If read() returns 0 (EOF), accesses buf[-1]; if returns -1 (error), accesses buf[-2]. If user sends exactly 0x20 (name) or 0x100 (guess) bytes without newline, no NUL is appended, causing subsequent strlen/printf/strcpy to over-read stack memory beyond the buffer.

attack_surfaces.input: username at base+0x2040 (0x20 bytes, no NUL if filled)
attack_surfaces.operation: printf('Hey %s. So you are now given 256 tries...', base+0x2040)
attack_surfaces.reason: printf %s reads name buffer as string with no length limit. If name is exactly 0x20 bytes without NUL, printf over-reads into base+0x2060 (2 bytes gap) and base+0x2060+ which contains uninitialized stack data. Confirmed at runtime: leaks 2 bytes (0x80 0x03 observed). This is a direct information leak of stack content.

attack_surfaces.input: guess at temp_buffer+0xa (0x100 bytes, no NUL if filled)
attack_surfaces.operation: strlen(temp_buffer) used as length for MD5_Update
attack_surfaces.reason: If guess is exactly 0x100 bytes without newline, no NUL is appended. strlen() then reads beyond the 0x10a-byte temp_buffer into adjacent stack data (md5_ctx at rbp-0x30f0 is below temp at rbp-0x1010). The extra bytes become part of the MD5 input, making the hash depend on stack content. Attacker controls whether this over-read occurs by sending exactly 0x100 bytes.

attack_surfaces.input: flag (47 bytes, no NUL) copied via strcpy to temp_buffer+0xa
attack_surfaces.operation: strcpy(temp+0xa, base) copies flag (47 bytes) plus stack garbage until NUL found
attack_surfaces.reason: flag.txt is read as exactly 47 bytes with no NUL terminator. strcpy copies flag bytes plus whatever follows on the stack until a NUL byte is encountered. This means MD5 is computed over flag + unknown stack garbage. The garbage content is not attacker-controlled but may be predictable or leakable.

attack_surfaces.operation: fread 1 byte from urandom, used as index: base + random_byte*0x10 + 0x40
attack_surfaces.reason: When score <= 127, leaks 16 bytes of MD5('attemptXX_' + flag + stack_garbage) at a random index (0-255). The index is not attacker-controlled (from /dev/urandom). The leaked hash contains flag data but also unknown stack garbage. Multiple runs leak different random hashes.

attack_surfaces.operation: strcpy(base+(i+0x104)*0x10, temp_buffer) overwrites loop1 hash with flag+garbage string
attack_surfaces.reason: strcpy copies temp_buffer (which contains 'attemptXX_' + flag + garbage + NUL) over the loop1 hash slot. This is part of the comparison logic, not directly attacker-controlled. The NUL termination at base+(i+0x5)*0x10 limits the copy length.

main allocates 0x30f0 bytes of stack. base = rbp-0x3090. Name at base+0x2040 (0x20 bytes). Loop1 hashes at base+(i+0x104)*0x10. Loop2 hashes at base+(i+0x4)*0x10.
main Loop1: 256 iterations, reads guess into temp+0xa (0x100 bytes), computes MD5('attempt%02x_' + guess) via strlen+MD5_Update, stores at base+(i+0x104)*0x10
main Loop2: 256 iterations, strcpy flag to temp+0xa, computes MD5('attempt%02x_' + flag+garbage), stores at base+(i+0x4)*0x10, then strcpy temp over loop1 hash slot, strcmp to compare
print_flag: if score > 127, prints flag via printf('%s', base). If score <= 127, reads 1 random byte from urandom, leaks 16 bytes of hash at base + random_byte*0x10 + 0x40
alarm(1) called before Loop2, signal(SIGALRM, sig_handler). sig_handler prints 'Too slow!' and exit(1).
Runtime confirmed: program prints 'Hello! What is your name?', echoes name, runs 256 guess prompts ('> '), then prints score and optionally a hash leak.
Runtime confirmed: with score=0, print_flag leaks 16-byte hex hash (e.g. 'a9a21c49d9722e5450fefe549da8e509') from a random index.
Name buffer at base+0x2040 is 0x20 bytes. If filled exactly without newline, printf('Hey %s...') over-reads past base+0x2060, leaking 2 bytes of uninitialized stack data (observed 0x80 0x03).
GOT is at 0x3f38 (0xc8 bytes). Full RELRO means GOT is read-only after relocation. 17 JUMP_SLOT entries for PLT functions.
No heap operations (malloc/calloc/realloc/free) found in the binary. All data is on the stack.

Loop2 uses strcpy to copy flag (47 bytes, no NUL) from base to temp+0xa. strcpy copies until NUL found, so it copies flag bytes plus stack garbage beyond the 47-byte flag until a NUL byte is encountered.
Loop2 overwrites loop1 hash slot (base+(i+0x104)*0x10) with temp_buffer content via strcpy, then NUL-terminates at base+(i+0x5)*0x10, then strcmp with loop2 hash (base+(i+0x4)*0x10).
libcrypto.so.1.1 imports dlopen@GLIBC_2.2.5 (UND symbol). No system/exec/popen found in libcrypto exports relevant to this binary's usage.

The 2-byte stack leak at base+0x2060 (between name buffer end at base+0x2060 and urandom FILE* at base+0x2070) reveals uninitialized stack content. The gap is 0x10 bytes (0x2060 to 0x2070), so up to 16 bytes could leak if no NUL is present.
The hash leak in print_flag uses random_byte as index into base+0x40 (loop2 hash array start). random_byte ranges 0-255, accessing base+0x40 to base+0x1040, which covers all 256 loop2 hash slots.

Loop2 hash = MD5('attempt%02x_' + flag + stack_garbage). The stack_garbage is whatever follows the 47-byte flag in the base buffer until a NUL byte. This garbage is from the stack frame and is not directly attacker-controlled.
